skills.label: A fraction splits a whole into equal parts
Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number
Writing a fraction in simplest form

equal-parts.q: A chocolate bar is cut into 4 pieces of the same size. One piece is what fraction of the bar?
equal-parts.explanation: Four equal pieces means each piece is one out of four, written 1/4.

equal-parts.q: Which picture shows a whole split into EQUAL parts?
options: A square cut into 4 same-size squares
A square cut into 4 random-size pieces
A circle with one tiny slice
A line split into 3 uneven bits
equal-parts.explanation: Fractions only work when every part is the same size.

multiply-both.q: Start with 1/2. Multiply the top and bottom by 3. What do you get?
multiply-both.explanation: 1×3 = 3 on top and 2×3 = 6 on the bottom, so 1/2 = 3/6.

multiply-both.q: To keep a fraction's value the same, you must multiply the numerator and denominator by…
multiply-both.explanation: Multiplying both parts by the same number keeps the quantity unchanged.

equivalence.explanation: Multiply top and bottom of 1/3 by 2 to get 2/6.
